newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore construction to grow by 6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Singapore construction to grow by 6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Singapore's construction industry is expected to award contracts worth S$17 billion (US$12 billion) in 1996, up 6 percent from $16 billion in 1995, according to Minister for National Development Lim Hng Kiang.
"Our construction industry is expected to grow strongly despite the general slowdown in the economy," Lim said in a speech at a dinner on Saturday.
He said that although the forecast for the construction sector remained rosy, such growth could not be maintained indefinitely as rising labour and building material costs posed a critical challenge.
"As the cost of doing business in Singapore goes up, we will lose our competitive edge," he said.
